The **Women's Team Archery** event at the **2012 Summer Olympics** in London was held from **27 to 29 July 2012** at **Lord’s Cricket Ground**. Here’s a detailed breakdown of the competition:

---

### **Key Details**
- **Venue:** Lord’s Cricket Ground, London
- **Dates:**
  - **Ranking Round:** 27 July 2012
  - **Elimination Rounds & Finals:** 29 July 2012
- **Format:**
  - **Ranking Round:** Each team’s total score was the sum of its three archers’ individual scores (72 arrows each, max 720 per archer).
  - **Match Play:** Best-of-24 arrows (6 arrows per set, 4 sets total). Teams earned **2 points per set win** (1 point each for a tie). The first team to **5 points** won. If tied at 4–4, a **single-arrow shoot-off** decided the winner.
- **Number of Teams:** 12 (36 archers total, 3 per team).

---

### **Qualification**
Teams qualified through:
1. **2011 World Archery Championships** (top 8 teams).
2. **Final Olympic Qualification Tournament** (June 2012, Ogden, USA).
3. **Host nation (Great Britain)** received an automatic spot.

**Qualified Teams:**
1. **South Korea** (World Champions)
2. **China**
3. **Chinese Taipei**
4. **Japan**
5. **India**
6. **United States**
7. **Italy**
8. **Russia**
9. **Mexico** (via final qualifier)
10. **Ukraine** (via final qualifier)
11. **Denmark** (via final qualifier)
12. **Great Britain** (host)

---

### **Ranking Round Results (27 July 2012)**
Teams were seeded based on the combined scores of their three archers in the **72-arrow ranking round**.

| **Rank** | **Team**         | **Score** | **Archers (Individual Scores)**                     |
|----------|------------------|-----------|----------------------------------------------------|
| 1        | South Korea      | 1993      | Ki Bo-bae (671), Lee Sung-jin (671), Choi Hyeon-ju (651) |
| 2        | United States    | 1979      | Miranda Leek (656), Khatuna Lorig (669), Jennifer Nichols (654) |
| 3        | Chinese Taipei   | 1976      | Tan Ya-ting (656), Lin Chia-en (662), Lei Chien-ying (658) |
| 4        | Mexico          | 1974      | Aída Román (658), Mariana Avitia (659), Alejandra Valencia (657) |
| 5        | Japan           | 1965      | Ren Hayakawa (665), Miki Kushida (646), Kaori Kawanaka (654) |
| 6        | Russia          | 1962      | Kristina Timofeeva (660), Inna Stepanova (649), Ksenia Perova (653) |
| 7        | China           | 1957      | Fang Yuting (651), Xu Jing (659), Cheng Ming (647) |
| 8        | India           | 1954      | Deepika Kumari (662), Laishram Bombayla Devi (651), Chekrovolu Swuro (641) |
| 9        | Italy           | 1950      | Natalia Valeeva (657), Jessica Tomasini (638), Pia Carmen Lionetti (655) |
| 10       | Ukraine         | 1947      | Kateryna Palekha (656), Lidiia Sichenikova (645), Tetyana Dorokhova (646) |
| 11       | Great Britain   | 1937      | Naomi Folkard (651), Amy Oliver (641), Alison Williamson (645) |
| 12       | Denmark         | 1931      | Louise Laursen (635), Maja Jager (655), Carina Christiansen (641) |

**Notes:**
- South Korea set an **Olympic record** (1993 points), breaking their own 2004 record (1991).
- The U.S. and Chinese Taipei were the only other teams to score above 1970.

---

### **Elimination Rounds (29 July 2012)**
#### **First Round (Round of 12)**
| **Match** | **Winner**       | **Score** | **Loser**        | **Score** |
|-----------|------------------|-----------|------------------|-----------|
| 1         | **South Korea**  | 210–192   | Denmark          | 192       |
| 2         | **China**        | 200–187   | Great Britain    | 187       |
| 3         | **Chinese Taipei** | 211–205 | Ukraine          | 205       |
| 4         | **Japan**        | 207–193   | Italy            | 193       |
| 5         | **Russia**       | 196–195   | India            | 195       |
| 6         | **Mexico**       | 210–209   | United States    | 209       |

**Upsets:**
- **Mexico** defeated the **U.S.** (seeded 2nd) in a **1-point thriller** (210–209).
- **Russia** edged out **India** by just **1 point** (196–195).

#### **Quarterfinals**
| **Match** | **Winner**       | **Score** | **Loser**        | **Score** |
|-----------|------------------|-----------|------------------|-----------|
| 1         | **South Korea**  | 221–213   | China            | 213       |
| 2         | **Japan**        | 206–199   | Chinese Taipei   | 199       |
| 3         | **Mexico**       | 214–209   | Russia           | 209       |

**Highlights:**
- **South Korea** dominated **China** (221–213), the highest score of the round.
- **Mexico** continued their upset run, beating **Russia** by 5 points.

#### **Semifinals**
| **Match** | **Winner**       | **Score** | **Loser**        | **Score** |
|-----------|------------------|-----------|------------------|-----------|
| 1         | **South Korea**  | 224–219   | Japan            | 219       |
| 2         | **China**        | 206–209   | **Mexico**       | **209**   |

**Key Moments:**
- **Mexico** stunned **China** (the 7th seed) to reach the final.
- **South Korea** set a **new Olympic record** (224 points in a match).

---
### **Medal Matches**
#### **Bronze Medal Match: China vs. Japan**
- **China** defeated **Japan** **209–208** in a **nail-biter**.
  - China led 2–0 after two sets but Japan tied it 4–4.
  - In the **shoot-off**, China’s **Fang Yuting** scored a **9**, while Japan’s **Miki Kushida** scored an **8**.

#### **Gold Medal Match: South Korea vs. Mexico**
- **South Korea** won **210–199** to claim their **7th consecutive Olympic gold** in women’s team archery.
  - South Korea led **4–0** after two sets (58–51, 57–53).
  - Mexico won the third set (55–53) but lost the fourth (57–52).
  - **Ki Bo-bae** (gold in individual) and **Lee Sung-jin** were dominant.

---
### **Final Standings**
| **Rank** | **Team**         | **Archers**                          |
|----------|------------------|--------------------------------------|
| **Gold** | **South Korea**  | Ki Bo-bae, Lee Sung-jin, Choi Hyeon-ju |
| **Silver** | **Mexico**      | Aída Román, Mariana Avitia, Alejandra Valencia |
| **Bronze** | **China**       | Fang Yuting, Xu Jing, Cheng Ming      |
| 4        | Japan           | Ren Hayakawa, Miki Kushida, Kaori Kawanaka |
| 5        | Chinese Taipei  | Tan Ya-ting, Lin Chia-en, Lei Chien-ying |
| 6        | Russia          | Kristina Timofeeva, Inna Stepanova, Ksenia Perova |
| 7        | United States   | Miranda Leek, Khatuna Lorig, Jennifer Nichols |
| 8        | India           | Deepika Kumari, Laishram Bombayla Devi, Chekrovolu Swuro |

---
### **Notable Performances & Records**
1. **South Korea’s Dominance**:
   - **7th straight Olympic gold** in women’s team archery (1988–2012).
   - **Ki Bo-bae** also won **individual gold**, becoming the first woman to win both events at the same Olympics since 1984.
   - Set **Olympic records** in ranking round (1993) and match play (224).

2. **Mexico’s Historic Run**:
   - First **non-Asian team** to reach the women’s team final since the event’s introduction (1988).
   - **Aída Román** (silver in individual) and **Mariana Avitia** (bronze in individual) led the team.

3. **Close Matches**:
   - **Mexico vs. USA (210–209)** and **Mexico vs. China (209–206)** were decided by **1–3 points**.
   - **Bronze medal** decided by a **1-point shoot-off**.

4. **Disappointments**:
   - **United States** (seeded 2nd) lost in the first round.
   - **India** (with world #1 **Deepika Kumari**) lost by **1 point** to Russia.

---
### **Aftermath & Legacy**
- **South Korea’s streak** continued until **2020 Tokyo**, where they lost in the quarterfinals (their first-ever Olympic defeat in the event).
- **Mexico’s silver** remains their best Olympic archery result.
- **Lord’s Cricket Ground** was praised for its unique setting, though windy conditions affected some matches.

---
### **Fun Facts**
- **Alison Williamson** (Great Britain) competed in her **6th Olympics**, a record for British archery.
- **Khatuna Lorig** (USA) later became famous as the archery coach for **Jennifer Lawrence** in *The Hunger Games*.
- The **gold medal match** was watched by **Prince William and Kate Middleton**.

---
### **Sources & Further Reading**
- [Olympics.com – London 2012 Archery Results](https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/london-2012/results/archery)
- [World Archery – 2012 Olympics Recap](https://worldarchery.sport/)
- [BBC Sport – Archery Coverage](https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/2012/sports/archery)
